Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: transaction categorization + merchant normalization for downstream reconciliation and analytics.
- Quality target: >= 95% schema-compliant structured outputs and <2% high-confidence misclassifications on the top 5 merchant categories.
- Constraints: PII in merchant names, strict JSON schema for downstream pipeline, occasional bursts during end-of-day processing.

Immediate recommendations (post-demo)
- Run the prompt set we captured during the call as a first eval (attached: finpay-eval-prompt-set.csv).
- We recommend running two model variants in parallel for the eval: redwood-7b-instruct (lower latency/cost) and redwood-14b-instruct-quant (higher quality). We'll surface per-model schema compliance and hallucination rates.
- For structured outputs, we recommend using our function-calling/structured output mode with an explicit JSON schema. This gives deterministic validation and clearer error signals for the eval.

Tech/ops asks from your side
- Can you confirm the sample volume for the pilot (we discussed ~2k transactions/day with 10k/day bursts)?
- Who should we send the access/IBR NDA and the SOW to? I attached a quick SOW draft for discussion.

Attachments: finpay-eval-prompt-set.csv, sow-draft-v1.pdf

Next steps (proposed)
1) FinPay runs the attached prompt set through both models (we can host or you can run locally) — due 2026-03-22
2) Redwood provides benchmark PDF with schema compliance, EM, and precision/recall for merchant canonicalization — deliverable 2026-03-25
3) Kickoff 2-week pilot focused on production-like traffic and retries/ingestion edge cases — target start 2026-04-05

1) JSON schema / structured output

2) Tool/function calling retries and idempotency

3) Benchmarks and drift/regression detection

4) Data handling and PII

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks for the great questions. I’m attaching the quick benchmark/export PDF (finpay-benchmarks-20260315.pdf) and summarizing answers below.

1) Example JSON schema (typical output)- We usually model merchant canonicalization as an object with the following top-level fields: 
  - merchant_id: string (optional)
  - merchant_name: string (required)
  - merchant_category: string (required, enum of 50 canonical categories)
  - normalized_merchant: string (required)
  - confidence_score: number (0-1, required)
  - evidence: array of strings (optional)

Runtime validation behavior- When function-calling/structured output mode is enabled, Redwood performs schema validation server-side. If an output fails validation we return a structured error block with: error_type (schema_validation), field_errors (list) and the raw model text. We do NOT silently mutate or guess — we return the failing payload so your pipeline can take deterministic actions.

2) Retry semantics and idempotency- Best practices: 
  - Use an exponential backoff with jitter for retries (we recommend starting at 500ms, doubling, max 8s, 3 attempts by default).
  - Include a request_id in the metadata so retries are idempotent from your side. Redwood will surface a request_id in responses; if you provide one we log it and it helps with debugging/traceability.
  - If a response fails schema validation, we recommend a single automatic retry. Many failures are whitespace/encoding issues or partial generations. If retry still fails, route to a deterministic fallback (rule-based extraction) or a dead-letter queue.

3) Benchmarks & regression detection- Out-of-the-box metrics we produce for structured evals: schema_compliance_pct, exact_match_pct (for normalized_merchant), precision/recall/F1 for category assignment, mean_confidence_by_category, and hallucination_rate.
  - Redwood Optimize can run your prompt set on a nightly cadence against pinned model versions and will alert on regressions (you can define thresholds per metric). We can add your FinPay prompt set to Optimize during the pilot.

4) Data handling & PII- Hosted runs: we treat inputs as transitory and we do not use customer data to train models. However, for regulated PII requirements we recommend Private deployment (VPC) — that’s what most customers doing merchant-level PII choose. I’ve noted this as a pilot decision item.

Recommended models for your eval- redwood-7b-instruct (baseline, low cost)- redwood-14b-instruct-quant (higher-quality quantized option)- If you need highest quality for canonicalization we can try a 30B-class variant for a subset of examples.

Quick implementation checklist for pilot
- Provide sample volume + credentials for S3 where we can pull the eval prompt set (or we can host temporarily)
- Confirm JSON schema (I attached a JSON schema snippet in the benchmark PDF)
- Provide PII constraints (if you need Private deployment we’ll scope infra in SOW)

Attachments: finpay-benchmarks-20260315.pdf

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up with your engineering team this week if helpful.
